data.text: Interactive system development involves specific cycles for gathering requirements, prototyping, and iterations across multiple stages. Implementation includes coding and systematic testing, followed by empirical studies to estimate usability. Because the traditional lifecycle is rigid and requires full completion and extensive documentation for each stage, the process can lead to significant time and cost overruns before deployment.
points: Requirement gathering, interface design, and code design involve specific cycles for gathering requirements, prototyping, and iterations.
Implementation includes coding and systematic testing, followed by empirical studies to estimate usability.
The traditional lifecycle is rigid because each stage requires full completion and extensive documentation before moving forward.
Because each stage takes a long time, this strict process can lead to significant time and cost overruns before deployment.

data.text: Agile development is a framework for fast development that starts small and reduces unnecessary documentation. It delivers features through successive deliveries, unlike the ISDLC method where the system is finished first. An agile sprint typically lasts four to six weeks and uses daily meetings and stakeholder feedback to make quick changes. While ISDLC helps understand the overall flow, agile methods are better for building practical products in a reasonable time frame.
points: Agile development is a framework for fast development that starts small and reduces unnecessary documentation.
Agile delivers features through successive deliveries, unlike the ISDLC method where the system is finished first.
An agile sprint typically lasts four to six weeks and covers requirements, development, testing, and delivery.
Teams maintain agility through daily meetings, live demonstrations, and frequent stakeholder feedback.
Agile methods are better for practical product development, whereas ISDLC is primarily for pedagogical purposes.

data.text: The book Human-Computer Interaction, User-Centric Computing for Design and the NPTEL course on the design and implementation of human-computer interfaces are recommended for further study. These resources cover concepts such as prototype building, prototype evaluation, empirical study, and agile methods.
points: Specific resources are recommended for studying prototype building, prototype evaluation, empirical study, and agile methods.
